title: D-087 3D-3: zero-dependency glTF 2.0 binary (GLB) writer - deterministic triangle-mesh export with named nodes, per-mesh materials and exact accessor bounds; validated by an in-test parser (module + tests; no route, no UI)
objective: Build services/api/app/cad/glb_writer.py: a dependency-free, deterministic writer of glTF 2.0 binary (GLB) files from a generic list of named triangle meshes (float positions in a declared local frame + uint32 indices + an optional base colour), producing one node per mesh, one material per distinct colour, exact accessor min/max, 4-byte chunk alignment, the JSON and BIN chunks, and an asset.generator + extras block carrying the CRS/unit/local-origin note and the 'Proposed - not a city record' label. Units: glTF is metres by specification, so the writer takes feet and converts with the declared US-survey-foot factor, recording it. Fail-closed typed refusals (non-finite values, out-of-range indices, degenerate meshes, size caps). The generic input keeps it independent of the massing model's evolving shape; wiring is a later packet.
business_reason: GLB is the runtime format the 3D architecture names for browser viewers and the most portable 3D interchange (D-087-R003/R006); a verified writer is the bridge from the massing truth object to any 3D view or download.

Every file path you write is under that worktree; commit your work there as ONE commit and report its sha. Never touch the primary checkout, the ledger, or any path outside allowed_paths.

ZERO NEW DEPENDENCIES (binding; D-087-R009 + the dependency-security policy): stdlib plus already-admitted packages only (shapely/numpy/pydantic/fastapi are admitted); no lockfile or requirements change; no network access in code or tests.

FORMAT AUTHORITY (binding; never guess): the Khronos glTF 2.0 specification (header magic 'glTF', version 2, chunk types JSON/BIN, 4-byte alignment with the specified padding characters, accessor componentType codes, bufferView targets, required asset.version '2.0'); cite sections, mark recalled ones '[recalled - verify]' for the G1 verifier. glTF units are metres and +Y up by specification - declare and apply the axis/unit mapping explicitly.

TESTS + MUTATION (binding): an in-test GLB parser validates header length, chunk alignment, JSON schema essentials, accessor counts/min/max against the input, and that the BIN chunk decodes back to the input (after the declared unit/axis mapping); golden sha256 for a fixed input; mutations - wrong padding character, accessor min/max off, a skipped unit conversion - each redden a named test.

Run `python tools/code_graph/query.py --no-regen impact <path>` before sweeps; graph ADVISORY - verify every material conclusion in actual source.

services/api/tests/cad/test_glb_writer.py - in-test parser, golden, mutation-sensitive tests
acceptance_scenarios: AS-1 (structure): valid GLB - 12-byte header (magic, version 2, total length), JSON chunk padded with spaces and BIN chunk padded with zeros to 4 bytes, asset.version '2.0'; byte-deterministic (golden sha256).

AS-2 (content): two named meshes with different colours round-trip through the in-test parser - node names, materials, index counts, positions (after the declared foot->metre and axis mapping) and accessor min/max all exact.

AS-3 (units + honesty): the foot->metre factor is the US survey foot (1200/3937) and is recorded with the CRS/local-origin note and the proposed-not-a-city-record label in asset/extras; mutation - skipping the conversion reddens.
AS-4 (fail-closed): non-finite values, index out of range, empty/degenerate meshes, over-cap vertex/index counts -> typed refusals, no partial output.
AS-5 (scope): zero new dependencies; not wired; ruff + modularity clean; exactly the allowed_paths change.
